changes.title: Does AI work for us, or do we work for AI?
26 Meta workers sue over alleged AI-aided layoffs targeting employees on medical or family leave
changes.summary: A group of 26 Meta employees has sued the company, claiming it used AI to choose people for layoffs, disproportionately targeting those on medical, parental or family leave.

changes.title: Google's AI search features pose 'unacceptable risk' to children, new report finds
changes.summary: Common Sense Media found that across more than 2,600 test interactions, Google's two built-in AI search functions routinely failed to recognize risky and harmful behavior.

changes.title: Battle against data centers grows nationwide amid concerns over electricity, water usage
changes.summary: There's growing backlash nationwide against AI data centers and now New York is hitting pause. Gov. Kathy Hochul signed an executive order to delay the building boom. Kelly O'Grady has more.

changes.title: The First Chatbot’s Multiple Personalities
changes.summary: ELIZA is remembered as the world’s first AI star, a kindly therapist in chatbot form that gently probed users’ worries. Even its creator, Joseph Weizenbaum, was surprised by the warm reception given to his experiment in human-machine interaction. changes.title: Highly fragmented European wetlands with uneven restoration needs
changes.summary: Nature, Published online: 15 July 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10760-9 Satellite imagery and machine learning used for the mapping of six seminatural open wetland types and land-use disturbance in European countries shows that wetlands are highly fragmented and have uneven restoration needs.

changes.title: Sustainability reports: What 10 years of corporate data reveal—and conceal
changes.summary: A new study finds that companies are increasingly disclosing climate data—yet coverage of value chains and social factors remains patchy. changes.summary: In science, researchers often focus their entire careers on the pursuit of one primary field.

changes.title: Product availability changed in Europe
changes.summary: AI is a fast-growing business expense. Some companies are cutting costs by switching to cheaper Chinese AI models. (Image credit: Imen Ben Youssef/Hans Lucas).

changes.title: Generative AI's power sparks fears of dumbing humans down
changes.summary: Generative AI chatbots capable of writing emails and computer code, translating, organizing a trip or coming up with gift ideas are now readily available, prompting some to ask whether human brainpower could suffer for lack of use.
